paths.intro: Begin with a short introduction to Imam Ali, place him among the Prophet's family and the Imams, then read his own words.

steps.why: An overview of the events before and on the day of Ashura.

paths.title: New to Shia Islam
paths.intro: A short reading order for someone starting from the beginning: first what Islam is, then what is particular to Shia Islam, then the core beliefs in more depth.

A summary of Islamic beliefs and ethics in fairly simple language.
A closer look at belief in God, prophets and the afterlife, once the basics are familiar.

records.title: Basic Teachings Of Islam
records.description: A book that the site says presents the essential beliefs and practices of Islam within the Shia tradition. Most of it is about God: His oneness, how people can know Him, and His relationship to humans and the universe. It then turns to fate and free will, prophets and revelation, the Quran, and the afterlife.
sample_questions: What does Islam teach about God?
Is there only one God in Islam?
What does Islam say about fate and free will?
Why do Muslims believe in prophets?
What does Islam say about paradise and hell?
Does Islam conflict with science?

records.title: Brief History of Fourteen Infallibles
records.description: A book from the World Organization for Islamic Services (WOFIS) that gives a brief history of the Prophet Muhammad, Lady Fatimah and the Twelve Imams, one by one, followed by a chronological list. The page gives no description of the work or its intended audience.
sample_questions: Who are the Fourteen Infallibles?
Who are the Twelve Imams?
What is the life story of Imam Ali?
Who was the Prophet Muhammad?
Who was Lady Fatimah?
Who was the Twelfth Imam?

records.title: The Core of Islam
records.description: A book that, in the site's words, aims to guide Muslims, especially young people, with clear answers to commonly asked questions. Its chapters cover the setting in which the Prophet Muhammad lived, core beliefs, what Muslims hold sacred, social behaviour, the position of women, the main groupings among Muslims, present-day issues, important days of the year, and prayer.
sample_questions: What are the core beliefs of Islam?
What are the main groups in Islam?
What does Islam say about women?
What are the important days in the Islamic year?
What is sacred to Muslims?
What issues do Muslims face today?

records.title: Discovering Islam
records.description: An introductory book on the basics of Islam from a Shia perspective, which the site says is especially useful for people new to Islam or thinking about becoming Muslim. It explains what Islam is and how one becomes a Muslim, the main beliefs (God, prophets, the Imams, the afterlife), everyday practices such as prayer and fasting, the Quran, and topics like family life and women in Islam.
sample_questions: What is Islam?
How do I become a Muslim?
What do Muslims believe?
Who are the twelve Imams?
What are the basic practices of Islam?
What does Islam say about family life?
I am new to Islam, where do I start?

records.title: Discovering Shi'i Islam
records.description: A short book that the site describes as a brief introduction to Islam in general and Shia Islam in particular. It covers where Shia Islam began, the sources Shias draw on (the Quran, the Prophet's example and his family), core beliefs, the main practices such as prayer and fasting, and Shia communities around the world.

Who are the Shia?

What do Shias believe?
What does the word Shia mean?
What are the main Shia practices?
Where do Shias live in the world?

records.title: Fatima The Gracious
records.description: A book by Abu Muhammad Ordoni that the site describes as a biography of Lady Fatimah, the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad. It covers her titles, her family life and her children, and in its later chapters the events after the Prophet's death, including the dispute over Fadak.

records.title: Fazail Ul-Mahdi
records.description: A book by Ali Akbar Talaafi that the site describes as a short biography of Imam al-Mahdi, the twelfth Imam, and a discussion of his reappearance, his lineage and the reasons for his occultation (ghaybah, his absence from public view). It also covers how believers should behave while waiting for him.

records.title: From Resolution to Revolution, the Message of Ashura
records.description: A book of talks that links the events of Karbala and Ashura to everyday moral and social questions. The site says it speaks to the needs of young Muslims, especially those living in the West. Topics include repentance, prayer as a spiritual practice, marriage, parenting, challenges facing youth, and the meaning of Ashura.

records.title: Islamic Teachings in Brief
records.description: A short book by Sayyid Muhammad Husayn Tabataba'i that the site describes as a summary of the teachings of Islam, written in relatively simple language. It covers belief in God, prophethood, the Qur'an, the Prophet and his family, the Imamate (the belief in leaders after the Prophet), the afterlife, ethics and religious commandments.

records.title: Karbala, the Chain of Events
records.description: An article that walks through the events leading to the battle of Karbala and the day of Ashura, when Imam Husayn, the Prophet's grandson, was killed. It gives background on the rulers Mu'awiya and Yazid, follows Imam Husayn's journey to Karbala and the battle itself, and ends with lessons drawn from it and a glossary.

records.title: The Mystery Of The Shi’a
records.description: A book that the site describes as a concise look at key aspects of Shia Islam, starting from the roots of the religion (core beliefs) and its branches (main practices). Later sections explain Shia practices that people often ask about, such as details of the call to prayer and the daily prayer and praying on a turbah (a small clay tablet), and include sayings about the Prophet's family.

It draws on Imam Ali's own sayings, sermons and letters from Nahj al-Balagha, a collection of his words, and includes a short autobiographical section and prayers.

records.title: Al-Kāfi (Vol. 1): The Sufficient
records.description: Al-Kafi is a collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) compiled by Shaykh al-Kulayni, shown here in Arabic with an English translation by Muhammad Sarwar. Volume 1 of 8 gathers narrations on intellect and ignorance, the virtue of knowledge, the oneness of God, and those with divine authority; this page also gives an overview of all eight volumes. It is a primary source, best suited to readers who already know the basics.

records.title: Al-Kāfi (Vol. 2): The Sufficient
records.description: Al-Kafi is a collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) compiled by Shaykh al-Kulayni, shown here in Arabic with an English translation by Muhammad Sarwar. Volume 2 of 8 gathers narrations on belief and disbelief, supplication (dua, calling on God), the excellence of the Quran, and social manners. It is a primary source, best suited to readers who already know the basics.

records.title: Al-Kāfi (Vol. 3): The Sufficient
records.description: Al-Kafi is a collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) compiled by Shaykh al-Kulayni, shown here in Arabic with an English translation by Muhammad Sarwar. Volume 3 of 8 gathers narrations arranged under books on ritual cleansing, menstruation, dying people, prayer and zakat (a religious charity payment). It is a primary source of narrations, not a guide to current rulings, and suits readers with some background.

records.title: Al-Kāfi (Vol. 8): The Sufficient
records.description: Al-Kafi is a collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) compiled by Shaykh al-Kulayni, shown here in Arabic with an English translation by Muhammad Sarwar. Volume 8 of 8, called al-Rawda (the Garden), is a miscellaneous collection that the site says includes long narrations from letters and wills of the Imams and historical reports, not arranged by topic. It is a primary source, best suited to readers with some background.

records.description: A collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq and arranged by the numbers mentioned in them, from one-numbered characteristics upward; shown in Arabic with an English translation by Dr. Ali Peiravi. According to the site the narrations range over history, doctrine, ethics and jurisprudence. It is a primary source for readers with some background.

records.description: A collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) about God, compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq and shown in Arabic with an English translation by Sayed Ali Raza Rizvi. According to the site it covers themes such as God's oneness and attributes, free will and predestination, and the nature of the Quran.
